title: Chicken Katsu with Rice
subtitle: crunchy panko chicken cutlets with a sweet-tangy katsu sauce, crisp cabbage and jasmine rice, Japanese diner style
imageAlt: Sliced golden panko chicken cutlet drizzled with dark katsu sauce beside rice and shredded cabbage on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Start the rice first; the cutlets take about 20 minutes.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Cutlets
steps.text: Slice each breast in half horizontally and pound to an even 1 cm. Season with the salt and pepper.

steps.title: Bread
steps.text: Coat each cutlet in the flour, then the beaten eggs, then press firmly into the panko on both sides.

steps.title: Katsu sauce
steps.text: Stir the ketchup, Worcestershire, soy sauce and sugar together until the sugar dissolves.

steps.title: Cabbage
steps.text: Toss the shredded cabbage with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium until a panko crumb sizzles right away. Fry 2 cutlets at a time, 3–4 minutes a side, until deep golden and 74°C (165°F) in the centre. Drain on a rack and rest 2 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Slice the cutlets into strips and serve with rice and cabbage, with the katsu sauce drizzled over.

fixIt.fix: Pat the chicken dry before flouring, and press the panko on firmly.
Wait for the oil to get hot enough, and fry in batches so it stays hot.
Add another teaspoon of sugar; Worcestershire brands vary.

saleTip: Buy chicken breasts in No Frills value packs and freeze breaded cutlets for a fast takeout night.
swap: Pork katsu (tonkatsu): boneless pork chops pounded to 1 cm, same method, to 71°C (160°F). Air fryer: spray the breaded cutlets with oil, 200°C 12–14 minutes, flipping halfway.
leftovers: Reheat cutlets in the oven or air fryer to keep them crisp.
doneness: Chicken cutlets at 74°C (165°F) in the centre (Health Canada, poultry pieces).
source: Based on tested chicken katsu methods (Just One Cookbook, America's Test Kitchen): pounded cutlets breaded in flour, egg and panko, shallow-fried, with a ketchup-Worcestershire-soy katsu sauce and shredded cabbage.
prepAhead: Bread the cutlets up to 4 hours ahead and chill uncovered on a rack.
Katsu sauce keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.
reheat: Cutlets on a rack at 200°C (400°F) for 10 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Crispy chicken and rice with katsu sauce; no cabbage.

fancy.note: Japanese-style curry sauce over the rice, mild and sweet.

addSteps.title: Curry sauce
addSteps.text: Melt the butter in a small pot over medium, stir in the flour and curry powder 1 minute, then whisk in the broth, honey and ketchup. Simmer 5 minutes until thick; spoon over the rice beside the katsu.

plating: Cutlet sliced and set back together on the rice.
A tall pile of cabbage beside.

why.0-5: Panko is the Japanese crumb katsu was made for: big flakes, extra crunch.
why.1-1: Worcestershire is the base of Japanese tonkatsu sauce, imported from Britain in the 1800s.
why.2-2: Raw shredded cabbage is the classic side; it cuts the richness of the fried chicken.

funFact: 'Katsu' is short for 'katsuretsu', the Japanese pronunciation of 'cutlet'.
airFryer: Air-fry the breaded cutlets in one layer at 200°C (400°F) for 10–12 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and 74°C (165°F). Lightly spray or brush the coating with oil first so it browns.
